text:
The Nifty 50 closed at 25,607.2, down 1.07% on the day, while the broader Nifty 500 slipped 0.57%. Both indices fell in a narrow range, with advances (251) barely outnumbering declines (244) and a breadth score of 62.7 indicating a “healthy” market but limited participation. The India VIX fell to 16.55, suggesting reduced volatility after the drop.

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) added INR 1,634.33 crore, extending a 21‑day buying streak, whereas Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) sold INR 556.42 crore. FIIs were net long on futures (22.1% long) but reduced contracts by 44 03 contracts. Sector‑wise, “leading” groups such as Realty, Banking, FMCG, Healthcare and IT held up, while “weakening” PSU banks, financial services and auto stocks lagged. Options data show a put‑call ratio (PCR) of 0.59 for Nifty, a max‑pain level near 25,700 and a call wall at 27,000, indicating modest bullish bias but resistance near that level.

Watch the Nifty 50 pivot points: support at 25,479, pivot at 25,694 and resistance at 25,822. A break below 25,479 could test the 200‑day moving average (24,003). For Bank Nifty, the key levels are 62,689 (S1), 63,310 (pivot) and 63,662 (R1). Keep an eye on crude oil prices (Brent $91) and the rupee (USD‑INR 92.98) as they may influence the next session’s direction.
